claims.text: Tesla Model S (Tesla owners manual) lists cargo volumes: front trunk 3.1 cu ft, rear trunk 25.0 cu ft (rear seats up), 61.4 cu ft with the rear seats folded, and maximum total cargo volume 64.6 cu ft.
BMW’s US technical specifications for the G60 5 Series list trunk volume as 18.4 cu ft for the 530i / 530i xDrive (the BMW i5 electric variant is listed as 17.3 cu ft).
Tesla Model S interior dimensions (per Tesla owner's manual): front legroom 42.4 in and rear legroom 35.5 in; front headroom 39.7 in and rear headroom 38.1 in.
BMW 5 Series (G60) interior dimensions (BMW technical specs): front legroom 41.3 in and rear legroom 37.0 in; front headroom 38.8 in and rear headroom 37.5 in.

Comparison of those OEM dimensions: the Model S gives slightly more front legroom (42.4 in vs. BMW 41.3 in) but the BMW 5 Series provides more rear legroom (37.0 in vs. Model S 35.5 in). (Sources: Tesla owner's manual; BMW technical specifications PDF.)
claims.published: Tesla owners manual (2026) and BMW press (May 24, 2023)
claims.about: Front/rear legroom comparison (Model S vs BMW G60)

claims.text: BMW's press materials state the new 5 Series seats were redesigned for a "noticeable increase in comfort" and the rear backrests fold 40:20:40 so the three elements can be folded individually or together to create additional cargo space for long items.
claims.about: BMW 5 Series — seat redesign and 40:20:40 folding rear seat

claims.text: Tesla's official owner's manual documents power seat controls that allow moving the seat forward/back and adjusting the seat’s height and tilt angle up/down, and it also includes a driver-seat calibration procedure (useful if the seat range appears limited).
claims.published: (owners manual PDF; see seat adjustment and calibration sections)
claims.about: Tesla Model S — seat adjustment / calibration documented

claims.text: Independent reviewer summary: reviewers note the Model S is very practical for cargo because of its hatchback/liftback design and generous folded-cargo volume, but several reviewers also describe the Model S rear-seat comfort as "adequate but not class-leading" versus German rivals (e.g., AutoEdgeView review).
claims.about: Model S — cargo practicality (hatch) and rear-seat comfort assessment
